records.name: Puebla
records.summary: Puebla led the national statistics for 2025 with 7 recorded killings of LGBT+ people, and trans women were 58.3% of all such killings nationwide that year across at least 17 states reporting victims - a top-of-table lethality record a visitor must weigh against any formal protections. Its legal gender recognition law (2021) still carries an 18-year minimum-age requirement that the Supreme Court voided in March 2022, and the state congress has still not corrected the text: for a visitor whose documents must match their presentation, the unmet duty to conform the law to the binding ruling is itself a live hostility signal, and no state-level enforcement data exists to temper it.

sources.summary: Quadratin (16 Jun 2026): of 60 LGBT+ people murdered in Mexico in 2025, 35 were trans women (58.3%), victims across at least 17 states; Puebla recorded the most of any state (7). The piece also notes documented educational and labour inequality against trans women as a standing condition.

HRW 'Gender Recognition in Mexico by State' (11 Mar 2025), Puebla row: the 2021 state congress passed a civil-code reform recognising the right to legal gender recognition and issued a corresponding implementing decree — the recognition regime the summary flags as still carrying the court-voided 18-year minimum.

records.name: Tripura
records.summary:
This state shows the country's clearest pattern of border-checkpoint profiling of gender-nonconforming presentation. In August 2024 police reported apprehending 15 people crossing the long, porous international border - including seven transgender people - in separate incidents within 24 hours, one group seized at a highway check post en route to the financial capital, some described by police as "disguised as third-gender" - the explicit frame that trans presentation is a cover for infiltration. A coordinated November 2024 sweep detained twelve more, including minors and transgender people. The state shares a long, porous international border, which sustains the checkpoint geography. These are named-state-actor operations with published counts, directly facing any trans-presenting visitor crossing by land.

sources.summary: Sentinel Assam: Tripura police apprehended 15 Bangladeshi nationals including 7 transgender individuals in separate incidents within 24 hours — bus search at Panisagar checkpoint, North Tripura, on the Assam-Agartala highway; detainees held fake Aadhaar/PAN cards, were en route Mumbai via Guwahati; Tripura shares a 856-km porous border with Bangladesh.

North East Today (2 Aug 2024): at the Panisagar check post, North Tripura district, police detained 7 Bangladeshi nationals — 2 transgender individuals and 5 others described as disguised as third-gender — travelling by bus to Mumbai; case of fraudulent documents and border-crossing routed through the highway checkpoint.

Sentinel Assam (9 Nov 2024): a joint 24-hour operation in Tripura detained 12 Bangladeshi nationals including minors and transgender people — first group of 6 (3 transgender persons) after midnight destined for Mumbai; second group of 6 with 3 children from Khulna at Udaipur Railway Station; local helper Md Hafizur arrested for facilitating movement.
